title: Culture Change: Bono's ONE Campaign Story
coreMove: Test whether a noble mission has changed the operating pattern underneath the message.
sourcePressure: Bono and the ONE Campaign extend culture-change logic into a mission-driven organization, where purpose language still cannot substitute for changed norms.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not invent ONE Campaign tactics, politics, fundraising, or internal programs.

sourceAnchors.name: Bono
sourceAnchors.detail: The source stabilizes Bono and the ONE Campaign as a mission-driven culture-change case after Lumeris.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bono brings the mission surface, but the lesson still has to stay underneath the rhetoric: changed norms require changed signals.

sourceAnchors.name: ONE Campaign
sourceAnchors.detail: The source uses the ONE Campaign as a comparative culture-change setting, while blocking invented tactics, politics, fundraising, or internal programs.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The ONE Campaign is the transfer test: purpose language can rise while the operating pattern still has to move.

hook: A team discovers OKRs in a conference room and suddenly gets aligned
A dashboard glows on a Monday morning and reveals the truth
A leader writes a goal on a whiteboard and everyone understands
opening with Culture Change: Bono's ONE Campaign Story as a definition rather than a pressure
counterintuition: Measurement is not bureaucracy, it is clarity
Goals are not dreams, they are systems
Accountability is not punishment, it is ownership
Bono is not a mindset, it is a system
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write three goals
Ask yourself what matters most right now
write one OKR without checking whether it changes behavior
examples: generic startup roadmap meeting with sticky notes
home chore chart with vague family goals
student group in a classroom choosing priorities
team lead reviewing a color-coded dashboard
